title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 34-37): Grothendieck is setting up an axiomatic, combinatorial 'analysis situs' (tame topology). The basic object is an 'atelier' (workshop): a set \(\mathcal F\) of 'figures' carrying three relations. These are \(\le\) (sub-figure), \(\ll\) ('strictly inside', roughly 'contained in the interior of') and a third, compatibility-type relation (the \(\pitchfork\) of p.35: two simplexes meet in a common face or not at all). Elementary figures ('multistructures', the set \(M\) of marked simplexes/cells) generate the others. There is a realization map \(p_{\mathcal F}=\mathrm{multens}\colon \mathcal F \to \mathrm{Fig}(L)\) into the figures of an actual space \(L \simeq E\). It sends a combinatorial figure to its underlying multistratified subset.

Page 36, step 1: the page completes the remark of p.35. One cannot expect \(\mathrm{mult}(F) \le \mathrm{mult}(G) \Rightarrow F \le G\), nor the analogue for \(\ll\). In examples 1.A and 1.B the opposite holds. Simplicial or combinatorial figures carry more data than their underlying sets. For instance, a pseudo-disc with a marked point needs a 'neighbourhood structure' along its boundary, and \(M \to \mathrm{Fig}(L)\) is not injective as soon as \(E\) contains an arc.

Step 2, Definition: \(\mathcal F\) is an *atelier ensembliste* (set-theoretic workshop) if three conditions hold:
- (a) \(p_{\mathcal F}\) is injective;
- (b), (c) \(p_{\mathcal F}\) reflects \(\le\) and \(\ll\);
- (d) \(p_{\mathcal F}\) reflects the third relation.

Then \(p_{\mathcal F}\) identifies \(\mathcal F\), with its structures, with a 'sub-atelier' of \(\mathrm{Fig}(L)\). He notes that the conditions are not independent. An added line says it amounts to the same as: \(\mathrm{mult}(F)\) elementary \(\Rightarrow F\) elementary.

Step 3, Definition of morphism of ateliers \(f\colon \mathcal F \to \mathcal F'\):
- (a) \(f\) is monotone for \(\le\) and \(\ll\) and sends \(\emptyset\) to \(\emptyset\);
- (b) \(f\) commutes with (finite?) infima for \(\le\).

Step 4: \(f\) is 'compatible with the structures' if (c) it sends elementary figures (multistructures) to elementary figures. The claim is that such an \(f\) is then equivalent to a map \(M \to M'\) of elementary pieces.

Step 5, margins: for \(F' = f(F)\) there is an induced map \(\tilde F \to \tilde F'\) and \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{formes}}(\tilde F) \to \mathcal P_{\mathrm{formes}}(\tilde F')\). In the examples \(\tilde F \to f(\tilde F)\) is injective, and in the 'set-theoretic cases' the induced map is monotone.

Page 37 continues with sub-ateliers: stability under sups of compatible families and intersections, versus closure under sub-figures, and strict vs non-strict sub-ateliers. Purpose: to define a category of combinatorial models of tame spaces with a realization functor to genuine subsets of a space, and to isolate when the combinatorial model is faithful.
errors: Condition (d), if read as \(\not\le\) (as transcribed), is just the contrapositive of monotonicity of \(p_{\mathcal F}\) and adds nothing. It must therefore be the compatibility/transversality relation of p.35 (\(\pitchfork\)), which makes the transcription suspect.

The morphism axiom (b) presupposes that finite infima for \(\le\) exist in an atelier. This is not part of the stated structure, and on p.37 he himself hesitates over which closure properties to impose.

The claim that a structure-compatible \(f\) is equivalent to a map \(M \to M'\) needs every figure to be determined by, and recoverable as, the sup of its elementary constituents, with \(f\) commuting with those sups. Only infima are imposed, so this is a gap; p.37 adds the condition that \(f_{\mathrm{sat}}\) of a figure is a figure.
The equivalence 'atelier ensembliste \(\iff\) (\(\mathrm{mult}(F)\) elementary \(\Rightarrow F\) elementary)' is asserted without argument and seems too weak to imply injectivity by itself.

ideas.what: Atelier: a set of figures with sub-figure order \(\le\), 'strictly inside' relation \(\ll\) and a compatibility relation, as a combinatorial, point-free model of tame geometric figures
ideas.modern_name: close to face posets / CW posets, o-minimal cell structures, and point-free (locale) topology with a 'well-inside' relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s–90s); 'well inside' and way-below relations: locale and domain theory (Scott 1972, Johnstone 1982)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology is announced in Esquisse d'un programme §5, but the 'atelier' formalism is unpublished

ideas.what: Atelier ensembliste: the realization map to Fig(L) is injective and reflects \(\le\), \(\ll\) and compatibility, so the atelier is a sub-atelier of an actual space's figures
ideas.modern_name: faithful / full embedding of a combinatorial structure into the lattice of definable subsets; geometric realization reflecting incidence

ideas.what: Observation that combinatorial figures (simplicial pieces, a pseudo-disc with marked point) are not determined by their underlying sets, so realization does not reflect order
ideas.modern_name: non-injectivity of geometric realization at the level of subsets; need for stratification or collar data

ideas.what: Morphism of ateliers: monotone for \(\le\) and \(\ll\), preserves \(\emptyset\) and finite meets; 'compatible with structures' if it sends elementary figures to elementary figures, then equivalent to a map of elementary pieces \(M \to M'\)
ideas.modern_name: meet-preserving poset maps / maps of frames or cell posets; maps of face posets inducing cellular maps

missed.claim: An axiomatic category of 'ateliers' (posets of figures with \(\le\), \(\ll\), compatibility) with a realization functor to figures of a space, and a criterion for when this realization is a faithful embedding. This is intended as a foundation for tame topology. The thread is left unsettled: which closure axioms, and whether morphisms are determined by elementary pieces.
missed.quote: On dit que \(\mathcal F\) est un atelier ensembliste si ... \(p_{\mathcal F}\) identifie \(\mathcal F\), avec les structures \(\le\), \(\ll\), ..., à un "sous-atelier" de \(\mathrm{Fig}(L)\)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a combinatorial, point-free alternative to o-minimal structures as a foundation for tame topology. The pairing of a sub-object order with a 'strictly inside' relation parallels the well-inside/way-below relations of locale theory. That parallel does not appear to have been drawn in the tame-topology literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page belongs to Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 attempt at an axiomatic analysis situs. Its notions (atelier, atelier ensembliste, morphism of ateliers) are absent from the literature, but on this page they remain tentative definitions with no theorem. The mathematics itself is fairly elementary order theory.
transcription_corrections: Line (d): the relation symbol is probably the third structure of p.35 (compatibility, written \(\pitchfork\) / a crossed relation), not \(\not\le\). As \(\not\le\) the condition would be vacuous. The same symbol recurs in 'avec les structures \(\le, \ll, \ldots\)'.
Previous page uses 'multicont(F)'; here the abbreviation reads 'multens' (multi-ensemble, i.e. underlying multistratified set). The reading is plausible but uncertain.
In the morphism definition the label 'f = f_Fig' is likely just '\(f\colon \mathcal F \to \mathcal F'\)' with 'Fig' as a subscript gloss.
